A deck you can build a level ON, not a boat you can put on a map. 477 tiles, and 376 of them are the joins.

A holystoned oak deck you can lay out. A bulwark that reads as standing up. A hatch you can open, a cargo hold under it, a great cabin aft, and the open sea she floats on.

Verdant 01 gave you a grassland. 04 gave you the coast. 10 gave the coast a harbour. This is the ship tied up alongside it.

The thing this pack does that the nautical shelf does not

Search "ship tileset" and most of what you find is a sprite: a vessel drawn as one picture, at one angle, at whatever size the artist chose. You can put it on your map. You cannot put your player on it, open a hatch, or send them below.

A ship is almost entirely boundaries. Deck meeting water. The bulwark standing up on that deck. A hole cut in the deck. A lid over the hole. A cabin threshold. A tarpaulin simply put down.

So the pack spends 376 of its 477 tiles on eight complete 47-mask autotile sets — six of them load-bearing in the sample map. A ship pack without them is a picture of a boat.

Set
Deck → open seaThe ship's edge over water. The signature — her outline, at any shape you draw.
Hull → open seaTarred strakes at the waterline, for a vessel seen from outside.
Bulwark → deckThe ship's side standing above her own deck. Faced — a lit cap, a shaded face, a cast shadow. This is what makes a deck read as somewhere you can stand.
Hold → deckThe open hatchway. Drawn as a hole, not a platform: dark coaming all round, cargo hold below.
Grating → deckThe grating that covers that same hatch, fitted flush into an oak coaming.
Cabin → deckThe great cabin's threshold — painted chequer floorcloth meeting the weather deck.
Tarpaulin → deckThe one soft edge aboard. Everything else on a ship was cut to a line by a shipwright; a tarpaulin's edge falls where it falls. Organic, with a contact shadow.
Deck → granite quayThe brow. Your deck meeting Verdant 10 Harbour's quay — composed here and shipped complete, so you do not need to own Verdant 10.

And almost every edge in it is hard. There is no soil on a ship: every surface was cut, planed, fitted and fastened, and a jittered edge anywhere on her would read as damage. Seven of the eight sets are hard. The exception is the cloth, and it is the exception on purpose.

25 objects, and every one ships twice or three times

Deck gear — capstan · ship's wheel · binnacle · mast heel and fife rail · mooring bitts · belaying pin rail Ordnance — long gun on a truck carriage · swivel gun · shot garland Stores — water cask · sea chest · flemished rope coil · corded cargo bale · powder barrel · casks stowed in chocks Rigging and canvas — furled course on its yard · spare spar on chocks · anchor cable flaked down Light and signal — deck lantern · ship's bell on its gallows Below decks — chart table · built-in bunk · galley stove In the water — ship's boat alongside · mooring buoy

Every prop ships in a transparent form and on the surface it belongs on, with the contact shadow between the two. Three of them ship in three files, on two different grounds. That is how 25 objects become 53 prop tiles, and it is a design decision rather than padding: a contact shadow has to darken something, so one drawn on transparency reads as a hole in your deck — but a pack that shipped only the grounded half would strand every buyer who has their own planking.

Animated

Four animated sea variants, three frames each, playing the sequence 0,1,2,1 — the ping-pong RPG Maker MZ's own water slot performs. Four and not one: a single animated water tile lays the same glint on every cell and reads as a lattice at map scale.

Plus a deck lantern, four frames, transparent and grounded. Its iron frame is byte-identical in every frame; only the flame moves.

What is proven, and what is not

This is the part most asset packs do not write down. Every claim here is produced by a command that runs against the files in this download.

  • Exact grid — all 477 tiles are exactly 16×16, every sheet a whole multiple of it.
  • Palette lock — every opaque pixel is one of the 51 declared colours. Not mostly. Every pixel. That is what makes tile 477 match tile 1.
  • No anti-aliasing — alpha is strictly binary. No halo, no soft upscale, no resampling anywhere.
  • Autotile completeness — all 8 sets carry all 47 masks: 376 mask slots, enumerated and compared. A blob set missing three tiles is broken in your map.
  • Godot — the shipped .tres was loaded headless in Godot 4.7.2 and Godot itself was made to COUNT: all 477 tiles built, every atlas source resolved, every multi-cell footprint exact. Scope: headless load and resource inspection — not the editor GUI, not a running game.
  • Tiled — every shipped .tsx was opened and rendered by Tiled 1.10.2's own tmxrasterizer and compared to the sheet you are downloading, tile by tile. The .tmx sample map renders pixel-for-pixel identical to the shipped PNG.
  • RPG Maker MZ — the A2 autotile sheet round-trips against MZ's own FLOOR_AUTOTILE_TABLE, parsed out of the engine's own rmmz_core.js rather than copied: 384 of 384 shapes byte-identical. It composes correctly against MZ's own autotile table.
  • The sheets match the loose tiles — the same art ships twice on purpose, and all 477 were compared and are identical.
  • The sample map is DATA — sample_maps/sample_map_01.json rebuilds the PNG byte-for-byte, and every id in it resolves in tiles.json.

What is NOT proven: seamlessness. Every tile's wrap boundary is measured against its own interior, and every 4×4 repetition is rendered and reviewed by eye — the fields ship in proof/repetition/ so you can look for the grid line yourself. That is a measured floor and a human review, and it is not a proof, so this page does not claim one. A statistical wrap test catches hard edge artefacts about 97% of the time and the commonest real defect only about 7%, because that defect damages the interior the test calibrates against. A weaker true claim beats a strong false one.

What you get

  • Loose tiles — tiles/16x16/, one PNG per tile, named by id
  • Sheets — one atlas per group; each autotile set is its own sheet in mask order
  • Godot — a .tres TileSet and its PNGs
  • Tiled — one .tsx per sheet, plus sample_maps/sample_map_01.tmx, a finished map you can open and edit
  • RPG Maker MZ — A2 autotile sheet, B and C object sheets, and a slots manifest
  • tiles.json — every tile with an id, role, material, sheet slot, tiling mode, autotile mask and animation frame
  • proof/repetition/ — the 4×4 fields, so you can check the tiling yourself
  • LICENSE.txt — commercial use permitted, no attribution required

Part of the Verdant series, which shares one 16px grid and one palette across every pack. Verdant 04 Tidewater, Verdant 10 Harbour and this pack are one continuous coastline: open shore, built harbour, ship alongside.
